purpose: machine-readable ontology for identifying and estimating causal effects from data as evaluable work units, selecting and defending an identification strategy (potential outcomes, DAGs, randomized vs quasi-experimental designs, confounding adjustment, sensitivity, mediation, transportability) as a subdomain node of quantitative/statistical analysis for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Causal Inference is modeled as a subdomain of quantitative/statistical analysis and causal inference.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable identification/estimation methods or decision areas, not generic statistics topics.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.

Scope follows the potential-outcomes (Rubin) and structural/graphical (Pearl) traditions and applied econometric/epidemiologic practice (Hernan & Robins 2020; Morgan & Winship 2014; Angrist & Pischke 2009).
exclusions: General statistical estimation and inference unrelated to causal identification (e.g., pure prediction, descriptive modeling).
Machine-learning model architecture and feature engineering except where used as nuisance estimators.
Data engineering, measurement-instrument construction, and survey logistics.
Reinforcement learning and online experimentation infrastructure beyond the randomized-experiment identification logic.

competency_questions.question: Given a substantive question, what is the well-posed causal estimand (treatment, outcome, population, contrast) it should be answered as?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAUSAL_QUESTION_FRAME maps question to an estimand

competency_questions.question: How is the estimand expressed as a contrast of potential outcomes and what assignment mechanism is assumed?
Which identifiability assumptions (ignorability, SUTVA, positivity) must hold and are they defensible for this data?
How does the assumed causal DAG license a backdoor or frontdoor identification strategy?
Which covariates must be adjusted for and which would introduce collider or mediator bias?
Given a valid control set, which adjustment estimator (matching, weighting, regression) fits the data and estimand?
When randomization is infeasible, which quasi-experimental identification strategy matches the available variation?
What licenses a causal claim from an experiment versus an instrumental-variable design?
Which natural-experiment assumption (parallel trends, continuity, pre-fit) does the chosen panel/threshold design rely on?
How is covariate balance and overlap verified before trusting an adjustment estimate?
How is uncertainty in the final causal estimate quantified given the design's dependence structure?
How robust is the conclusion to a plausible unmeasured confounder?
How is a total effect decomposed into mechanism (direct/indirect) components?
Does an internally valid effect transport to the target population, and under what conditions?

glossary.definition: the precise causal quantity targeted, a contrast of potential outcomes on a named population
a common cause of treatment and outcome that opens a backdoor path
a variable that is a common effect of two others; conditioning on it opens a path
treatment is independent of potential outcomes given measured covariates
every covariate stratum has a nonzero probability of each treatment level
no interference between units and a single version of treatment
a graphical rule for choosing a covariate set that blocks all confounding paths
the local average treatment effect identified for compliers in an IV design
treated and control groups would have followed the same outcome path absent treatment
the probability of treatment given covariates, a one-dimensional balancing score
the minimum confounder-outcome and confounder-treatment association needed to explain away an effect
the conditions under which a causal effect generalizes to a different target population

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established causal-inference literature (Pearl 2009; Hernan & Robins 2020; Morgan & Winship 2014; Angrist & Pischke 2009) and methodological practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Define the causal question as a well-posed estimand: treatment, outcome, target population, and contrast (ATE/ATT/CATE) before any data analysis.
contradictors: analyst who fits a model before defining the estimand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when treatment/outcome definition or target population changes

pros.claim: an explicit estimand prevents estimator-question mismatch downstream
pros.example: specify ATT under a target-trial protocol instead of a vague 'effect of X'

cons.claim: an ill-posed estimand makes every later identification step undefined
cons.example: 'effect of obesity' with no time-zero yields incomparable contrasts

acceptance_tests: estimand stated as a contrast of potential outcomes on a named population
treatment, outcome, and time-zero unambiguously defined
revisit_triggers: decision context changes which contrast matters

nodes.definition: Express the causal effect via Rubin's potential-outcomes model: each unit has counterfactual outcomes Y(1),Y(0) and the effect is their contrast.
contradictors: analyst who equates regression coefficients with effects without counterfactual framing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the assignment mechanism or contrast definition changes

pros.claim: provides the precise target every estimator approximates
pros.example: ATT = E[Y(1)-Y(0) | treated]

cons.claim: the missing counterfactual must be supplied by assumptions, not data alone
cons.example: only Y(1) observed for treated, Y(0) for untreated

failure_modes: treating observed difference as the causal contrast without identification
ignoring the fundamental problem of causal inference
acceptance_tests: estimand written as a contrast of potential outcomes

nodes.definition: State and defend the assumptions that license replacing counterfactuals with observable quantities: ignorability/exchangeability, SUTVA/consistency, and positivity/overlap.
contradictors: analyst who assumes 'controlling for covariates' suffices without checking positivity or interference

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new unmeasured common cause, interference, or positivity violation is discovered

pros.claim: makes the leap from association to causation auditable
pros.example: conditional exchangeability + positivity license backdoor adjustment

cons.claim: assumptions are untestable from data alone and easily overstated
cons.example: assuming no unmeasured confounding when an obvious common cause is unrecorded

failure_modes: SUTVA broken by interference or multiple treatment versions
acceptance_tests: each identifiability assumption stated and justified

nodes.definition: Encode the assumed data-generating structure as a directed acyclic graph / structural causal model to make confounders, mediators, and colliders explicit.
contradictors: regression modeler who selects controls by p-value rather than causal structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new variable, arrow, or mechanism is added to the assumed structure

pros.claim: turns identification into a graphical, checkable procedure
pros.example: backdoor sets read directly off the DAG

cons.claim: a wrong DAG silently licenses the wrong adjustment set
cons.example: omitting an arrow into the treatment hides a confounder

failure_modes: DAG drawn to justify a desired result
acceptance_tests: DAG is acyclic and includes plausible common causes
implied conditional independences listed for testing

nodes.definition: Use the backdoor criterion and d-separation to choose a covariate set that blocks all confounding paths, enabling unbiased adjustment.
contradictors: analyst who adjusts for everything available ('kitchen-sink' control)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the DAG changes or a chosen control is reclassified as a mediator/collider

pros.claim: yields a defensible, minimal adjustment set rather than ad hoc controls
pros.example: adjust for the confounder but not the mediator on the causal path

cons.claim: adjusting for a mediator or collider introduces bias
cons.example: conditioning on a post-treatment variable blocks part of the effect

failure_modes: incomplete blocking of a backdoor path
acceptance_tests: chosen set blocks every backdoor path

nodes.definition: Identify a causal effect through a fully-mediating mechanism using the frontdoor criterion when no valid backdoor adjustment set exists.
contradictors: analyst who abandons identification when confounders are unmeasured
inputs: DAG showing a fully mediating path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the mediator is found to be incompletely mediating or itself confounded

pros.claim: recovers identification when backdoor fails but a clean mechanism is observed
pros.example: estimate the effect via a measured biological mediator

cons.claim: requires a fully-mediating, unconfounded mechanism that is rare in practice
cons.example: an unblocked confounder on the mediator path invalidates frontdoor

failure_modes: mediator only partially mediates the effect
acceptance_tests: no unblocked confounding of mediator paths

nodes.definition: Detect and avoid bias induced by conditioning on colliders or on a selected/censored sample (M-bias, selection bias, Berkson's paradox).
contradictors: analyst who treats any 'significant' covariate as a confounder to control

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when sample selection or a new conditioning variable is introduced

pros.claim: prevents 'controlling for' a variable that creates rather than removes bias
pros.example: not conditioning on a common effect of treatment and outcome

cons.claim: collider bias is invisible to standard fit statistics and easy to introduce
cons.example: selecting on hospitalized patients induces a spurious association

failure_modes: Berkson-type bias in a clinical sample
acceptance_tests: no collider conditioned in the adjustment set
selection mechanism assessed for induced association

nodes.definition: Classify each candidate covariate as confounder, mediator, collider, instrument, or noise to build a valid control set and avoid bad controls.
contradictors: analyst who maximizes R-squared by adding all available covariates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a covariate's causal role is reclassified or a new covariate is added

pros.claim: separates good controls from bias-inducing bad controls
pros.example: drop the mediator and the post-treatment proxy from the control set

cons.claim: role classification depends on an assumed structure that may be wrong
cons.example: mislabeling a confounder as a mediator drops a needed control

acceptance_tests: each covariate assigned a causal role
no post-treatment bad controls in the set

nodes.definition: Design a randomized experiment (RCT/A-B test) so random assignment guarantees exchangeability and identifies the effect with minimal modeling assumptions.
contradictors: observational-only analyst who treats RCTs as always infeasible

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when randomization integrity is threatened by noncompliance or attrition

pros.claim: randomization makes treatment groups exchangeable in expectation, minimizing assumptions
pros.example: balanced covariates by design remove confounding

cons.claim: noncompliance, attrition, and external-validity limits can still bias or narrow conclusions
cons.example: per-protocol analysis reintroduces selection bias

nodes.definition: Identify effects under unmeasured confounding using an instrument that affects treatment but the outcome only through treatment; estimate LATE/2SLS.
contradictors: analyst who uses any correlated variable as an instrument

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when instrument relevance weakens or an exclusion-restriction violation is suspected

pros.claim: recovers causal effects despite unmeasured confounding when a valid instrument exists
pros.example: draft-lottery instrument for the effect of military service

cons.claim: weak instruments and exclusion violations produce severely biased estimates
cons.example: an instrument with a direct outcome path breaks identification

nodes.definition: Exploit a treatment-assignment threshold on a running variable to identify a local effect at the cutoff (sharp or fuzzy RDD).
contradictors: analyst who extrapolates RDD effects far from the cutoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when running-variable manipulation or bandwidth sensitivity is detected

pros.claim: delivers credible local identification near a known threshold
pros.example: test-score cutoff for a scholarship's effect

cons.claim: identifies only a local effect and assumes no manipulation at the cutoff
cons.example: bunching just above the threshold signals gaming

acceptance_tests: continuity of covariates at cutoff checked

nodes.definition: Estimate effects of a treatment that turns on at a known time by comparing treated vs control pre/post changes under a parallel-trends assumption.
contradictors: analyst who ignores pre-trends and staggered-adoption bias

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when pre-trends diverge or treatment timing is staggered across units

pros.claim: differences out time-invariant confounders via the pre/post comparison
pros.example: policy adopted in some states but not others

cons.claim: parallel-trends is untestable post-treatment and staggered adoption biases two-way FE
cons.example: negative weights in TWFE with heterogeneous timing

acceptance_tests: pre-trends shown parallel via event study

nodes.definition: Construct a weighted combination of control units that reproduces a single treated unit's pre-treatment trajectory to estimate its counterfactual.
contradictors: analyst who applies synthetic control without pre-fit or placebo checks

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when pre-treatment fit is poor or the donor pool is contaminated

pros.claim: provides a transparent, data-driven counterfactual for a single aggregate unit
pros.example: synthetic control for one state's policy effect

cons.claim: relies on good pre-fit and an uncontaminated donor pool; inference is permutation-based
cons.example: poor pre-period fit invalidates the counterfactual

failure_modes: donor pool affected by the treatment

nodes.definition: Estimate each unit's probability of treatment given covariates as a balancing score that reduces high-dimensional confounding to one dimension.
contradictors: analyst who includes instruments or colliders in the propensity model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when overlap fails or covariate balance after conditioning is poor

pros.claim: collapses many confounders into one balancing score for matching/weighting
pros.example: one score balances dozens of covariates between groups

cons.claim: only balances measured confounders and is sensitive to model misspecification and overlap
cons.example: including a collider in the score reintroduces bias

failure_modes: bad controls in the score model
balance assessed by p-values rather than SMDs
acceptance_tests: only confounders included in the score

nodes.definition: Pair or group treated and control units with similar covariates or propensity scores to approximate a randomized comparison.
contradictors: analyst who reports matched results without checking post-match balance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when matched balance is inadequate or many treated units are unmatched

pros.claim: yields an interpretable, balanced comparison set approximating an experiment
pros.example: nearest-neighbor matching on the propensity score for ATT

cons.claim: discards unmatched units and depends on caliper/algorithm choices
cons.example: pruning treated units changes the estimand

failure_modes: caliper chosen to favor a result

nodes.definition: Reweight units by the inverse of their treatment probability (IPW) and combine with outcome modeling for doubly-robust (AIPW/TMLE) estimation.
contradictors: analyst who ignores extreme weights from near-zero propensities

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when weights become extreme or the propensity/outcome models are misspecified

pros.claim: doubly-robust estimators are consistent if either the treatment or outcome model is correct
pros.example: AIPW protects against one misspecified nuisance model

cons.claim: extreme weights inflate variance and small propensities destabilize estimates
cons.example: a propensity near zero produces a huge, unstable weight

nodes.definition: Estimate effects by modeling the outcome conditional on treatment and confounders and standardizing (g-formula) over the covariate distribution.
contradictors: analyst who interprets a covariate-adjusted coefficient as a causal effect under time-varying confounding

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when functional-form misspecification or time-varying confounding is suspected

pros.claim: uses the outcome model efficiently and standardizes to the target population
pros.example: g-formula handles time-varying treatments where naive regression fails

cons.claim: biased under functional-form misspecification and time-varying confounding affected by prior treatment
cons.example: conditioning on a time-varying confounder blocks part of the effect

acceptance_tests: marginal effect obtained by standardization not just a coefficient

nodes.definition: Quantify how strong an unmeasured confounder would have to be to overturn the estimated effect (E-value, Rosenbaum bounds, bias formulas).
contradictors: analyst who reports a point estimate as definitive without robustness bounds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a plausible unmeasured confounder stronger than the bound is identified

pros.claim: converts the untestable no-confounding assumption into a quantified robustness claim
pros.example: an E-value of 1.2 means weak confounding could explain the result

cons.claim: bounds depend on the assumed confounding model and can be misread as proof of robustness
cons.example: a large E-value still does not rule out a specific strong confounder

acceptance_tests: tipping point relative to plausible confounders assessed
assumptions of the sensitivity model stated

nodes.definition: Decompose a total effect into direct and indirect components (natural/controlled direct and indirect effects) under cross-world mediation assumptions.
contradictors: analyst who uses Baron-Kenny product-of-coefficients ignoring confounding

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a mediator-outcome confounder or exposure-mediator interaction is found

pros.claim: answers mechanism questions beyond the total effect
pros.example: how much of treatment effect runs through the mediator

cons.claim: requires strong cross-world assumptions and no mediator-outcome confounding
cons.example: an unmeasured mediator-outcome confounder biases the decomposition

acceptance_tests: natural direct/indirect effects identified under stated assumptions

nodes.definition: Assess whether and how a causal effect estimated in one population/setting transfers to a target population using selection diagrams and reweighting.
contradictors: analyst who assumes an internally valid effect automatically generalizes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the target population's effect-modifier distribution differs from the source

pros.claim: makes generalization an explicit, checkable transport problem
pros.example: reweight a trial effect to a real-world target population

cons.claim: requires correct effect modifiers and overlap between source and target distributions
cons.example: an unmeasured effect modifier breaks transport

nodes.definition: Produce the final causal estimate with valid uncertainty (standard errors, bootstrap, clustering) and translate it into a defensible causal claim.
contradictors: analyst who reports a point estimate without correct uncertainty or with naive SEs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the dependence structure (clustering/serial correlation) or estimator changes

pros.claim: ties the estimate to honest uncertainty and a claim no stronger than identification allows
pros.example: cluster-robust SEs when treatment is assigned at the group level

cons.claim: ignoring dependence or estimation uncertainty overstates precision and the causal claim
cons.example: naive SEs under clustered assignment understate uncertainty

failure_modes: causal claim stronger than identification supports
acceptance_tests: claim scope matches the identified estimand

edges.why_related: the estimand defines which potential-outcome contrast is targeted
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing the effect before the estimand yields an undefined contrast
edges.example: ATT vs ATE chosen before notation
edges.resolution_rule: fix the estimand before formalizing potential outcomes

edges.why_related: counterfactual contrasts require identifying assumptions to be estimable
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping assumptions leaves the estimand unidentified
edges.example: ignorability stated for the chosen contrast
edges.resolution_rule: state assumptions immediately after the potential-outcomes setup

edges.why_related: a DAG operationalizes and tests the identifying assumptions
edges.risk_of_conflict: asserting assumptions without a structure hides confounders
edges.example: DAG encodes no-unmeasured-confounding claim
edges.resolution_rule: draw the DAG to encode the stated assumptions

edges.why_related: the DAG determines valid backdoor adjustment sets
edges.risk_of_conflict: adjusting without the DAG risks bad controls
edges.example: backdoor set read off the DAG
edges.resolution_rule: derive the adjustment set from the finalized DAG

edges.why_related: frontdoor identification requires a DAG with a fully-mediating path
edges.risk_of_conflict: frontdoor without a verified mechanism is invalid
edges.example: frontdoor used when backdoor set unavailable
edges.resolution_rule: apply frontdoor only after the DAG confirms full mediation

edges.why_related: the DAG reveals colliders and selection nodes to avoid conditioning on
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing the collider structure induces selection bias
edges.example: collider flagged before building the control set
edges.resolution_rule: classify colliders from the DAG before adjustment

edges.why_related: backdoor analysis drives the covariate-role classification
edges.risk_of_conflict: classifying covariates without backdoor logic mislabels controls
edges.example: covariate roles assigned from backdoor paths
edges.resolution_rule: run confounding diagnosis using the backdoor adjustment set

edges.why_related: the validated confounder set feeds the propensity model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balancing score on the right covariates
edges.risk_of_conflict: a propensity model on bad controls reintroduces bias
edges.example: only confounders enter the propensity model
edges.resolution_rule: build the propensity score from the diagnosed confounder set

edges.why_related: outcome regression standardizes over the diagnosed confounder set
edges.risk_of_conflict: regressing on bad controls biases the standardized effect
edges.example: g-formula over the confounder set
edges.resolution_rule: regress/standardize only on the confirmed control set

edges.why_related: matching pairs units on the estimated propensity score
edges.risk_of_conflict: matching before a valid score yields imbalance
edges.example: nearest-neighbor on the propensity score
edges.resolution_rule: estimate the propensity score before matching

edges.why_related: IPW weights are functions of the estimated propensity score
edges.risk_of_conflict: weighting on a misspecified score destabilizes estimates
edges.example: IPW weight = 1/propensity
edges.resolution_rule: fit and diagnose the propensity score before computing weights

edges.why_related: randomization is the design that makes ignorability hold by construction
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing a trial without an estimand wastes the strongest design
edges.example: RCT chosen to guarantee exchangeability
edges.resolution_rule: prefer randomization when it can satisfy the assumptions directly

edges.why_related: IV substitutes an exclusion-restriction assumption for ignorability
edges.risk_of_conflict: using IV without checking its assumptions biases the estimate
edges.example: IV chosen when confounders are unmeasured
edges.resolution_rule: adopt IV only after its relevance/exclusion assumptions are defended

edges.why_related: RDD relies on continuity at the threshold as its identifying assumption
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying RDD without a real cutoff is invalid
edges.example: RDD at a known assignment threshold
edges.resolution_rule: use RDD only where a genuine threshold rule exists

edges.why_related: DiD relies on a parallel-trends identifying assumption
edges.risk_of_conflict: DiD without parallel trends is biased
edges.example: DiD for a policy turning on at a date
edges.resolution_rule: adopt DiD only with credible parallel-trends evidence

edges.why_related: synthetic control generalizes DiD to a weighted single-unit counterfactual
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic control without pre-fit mimics a failed DiD
edges.example: synthetic control when one unit is treated
edges.resolution_rule: use synthetic control when DiD's single-unit case needs weighting

edges.why_related: sensitivity analysis quantifies departures from the identifying assumptions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: robustness bound on the no-confounding claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting an effect without sensitivity hides fragility
edges.example: E-value computed for the no-confounding assumption
edges.resolution_rule: run sensitivity analysis against the stated assumptions

edges.why_related: mediation decomposition needs control of mediator-outcome confounding from the DAG
edges.risk_of_conflict: mediation without confounder control is uninterpretable
edges.example: natural direct/indirect effects under mediator confounder control
edges.resolution_rule: decompose only after mediator-outcome confounders are controlled

edges.why_related: transport adds selection-difference assumptions to the identification set
edges.risk_of_conflict: assuming transport without selection analysis overgeneralizes
edges.example: reweight a trial effect to a target population
edges.resolution_rule: perform transport analysis on top of internal identification

edges.why_related: final estimation must respect the identified estimand and its assumptions
edges.risk_of_conflict: estimating before identification produces an uninterpretable number
edges.example: CI reported for the identified ATT
edges.resolution_rule: estimate and quantify uncertainty only for the identified estimand

edges.why_related: the trial design dictates the estimator and clustering for inference
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring assignment level understates uncertainty
edges.example: cluster-robust SEs for cluster-randomized trials
edges.resolution_rule: match the inference procedure to the randomization unit

edges.why_related: IV/2SLS requires appropriate (often weak-instrument-robust) inference
edges.risk_of_conflict: naive IV SEs misstate precision with weak instruments
edges.example: Anderson-Rubin intervals for weak IV
edges.resolution_rule: use IV-appropriate inference after estimation

edges.why_related: collider/selection structure limits which covariates may be controlled
edges.risk_of_conflict: controlling a collider flips a clean diagnosis into a biased one
edges.example: exclude a collider from the control set
edges.resolution_rule: let collider analysis constrain the diagnosed control set

edges.why_related: both are graphical identification routes selected from the DAG
edges.risk_of_conflict: confusing the two applies the wrong adjustment formula
edges.example: frontdoor vs backdoor chosen by available paths
edges.resolution_rule: choose frontdoor only when no valid backdoor set exists

edges.why_related: tight randomized control buys internal validity at the cost of external generalizability
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming both strong internal and external validity from one RCT overreaches
edges.example: an efficacy RCT in a narrow sample
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize the validity the decision needs; report the conceded one as a limitation

edges.why_related: IV trades bias-reduction under unmeasured confounding for higher variance and a local estimand versus efficient regression
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing the two without justification yields conflicting effects
edges.example: noisy LATE vs precise but confounded OLS
edges.resolution_rule: choose IV when unmeasured confounding dominates; regression when overlap and ignorability hold

edges.why_related: matching discards units for interpretability while weighting keeps all units at the cost of variance
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting both with different estimands confuses the conclusion
edges.example: pruned matched ATT vs full-sample IPW ATE
edges.resolution_rule: pick the estimator whose estimand and overlap properties match the question

edges.why_related: an assumed DAG can encode untestable assumptions that overstate identifiability
edges.risk_of_conflict: a convenient DAG can manufacture identification that the data cannot support
edges.example: adding an arrow to justify a desired adjustment
edges.resolution_rule: when DAG and assumptions disagree, defer to substantive knowledge and test implied independences

edges.why_related: a precise adjusted estimate competes with the humility a sensitivity bound imposes
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting a tight CI while hiding sensitivity overstates certainty
edges.example: narrow CI but small E-value
edges.resolution_rule: report the estimate together with its robustness bound, not in place of it

edges.why_related: pressure to report a precise number competes with answering the originally framed estimand
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps the claim aligned to the question
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimizing an estimator for a different estimand answers the wrong question
edges.example: switching to an easier estimand for a tighter CI
edges.resolution_rule: the framed estimand dominates estimator convenience

edges.why_related: a clean DiD point estimate competes with the doubt raised by pre-trend/robustness checks
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forces honest reporting of assumption risk
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring pre-trend tests overstates DiD credibility
edges.example: significant DiD with a borderline pre-trend
edges.resolution_rule: report DiD effects only with pre-trend and robustness evidence attached

edges.why_related: the estimand bounds which variables and mechanisms the DAG must include
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unfocused DAG wastes effort on irrelevant structure
edges.example: DAG scoped to the treatment-outcome question
edges.resolution_rule: scope the DAG to the framed estimand

edges.why_related: noncompliance/attrition in a trial triggers sensitivity analysis of its assumptions
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-analysis loops if no stop rule
edges.example: sensitivity bounds for differential dropout
edges.resolution_rule: run one sensitivity pass per detected randomization breach; stop when bounds are reported

edges.why_related: an estimate that cannot answer the framed question triggers re-framing the estimand
edges.risk_of_conflict: infinite reframing loops without a stop condition
edges.example: estimate identifies LATE but question wanted ATE
edges.resolution_rule: reframe at most once per cycle; stop when estimand and estimate match

edges.why_related: collider/selection structure constrains which covariates may enter the propensity model
edges.risk_of_conflict: a collider in the score reintroduces selection bias
edges.example: exclude colliders from the propensity model
edges.resolution_rule: let collider analysis restrict the propensity covariate set

edges.why_related: transported estimates need uncertainty that reflects the reweighting
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring reweighting variance understates uncertainty
edges.example: bootstrap over the transport weights
edges.resolution_rule: propagate transport-weight uncertainty into the final interval

edges.why_related: mediation rests on strong assumptions that demand a sensitivity analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting NDE/NIE without sensitivity overstates mechanism certainty
edges.example: sensitivity to mediator-outcome confounding
edges.resolution_rule: attach a sensitivity analysis to every mediation decomposition

edges.why_related: IPW/AIPW require influence-function or bootstrap inference
edges.risk_of_conflict: plug-in SEs ignore weight-estimation uncertainty
edges.example: influence-function SEs for AIPW
edges.resolution_rule: use estimator-appropriate variance for weighted estimates

edges.why_related: matched-sample inference must account for the matching design
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating matched data as iid understates uncertainty
edges.example: matching-adjusted standard errors
edges.resolution_rule: use matching-aware inference after building the matched sample

edges.why_related: RDD requires bandwidth-robust, bias-corrected inference
edges.risk_of_conflict: conventional SEs over-reject near the cutoff
edges.example: robust bias-corrected RDD intervals
edges.resolution_rule: use bias-corrected RDD inference after estimation

conflict_axes.trigger: tightening identification reduces generalizability to the target population
resolution_order: identify the decision's primary inferential target
prioritize the validity that target demands
document the conceded validity as a limitation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the validity type required by the decision dominates; the conceded type is reported as a bounded limitation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: study claims both strong causal and strong population inference at once
conflict_axes.example: an efficacy RCT in a narrow sample applied to a broad population

conflict_axes.trigger: methods that remove confounding bias often inflate variance and narrow the estimand
resolution_order: assess whether unmeasured confounding is plausible
if yes prefer the bias-robust design
if no prefer the efficient adjustment estimator
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: when unmeasured confounding is credible, bias-robust identification dominates efficiency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a weak instrument yields a near-uninformative interval
conflict_axes.example: noisy LATE from a weak IV vs precise but possibly confounded OLS

conflict_axes.trigger: adding controls reduces confounding but risks conditioning on mediators or colliders
resolution_order: classify each covariate's causal role
include confounders, exclude mediators/colliders
document excluded bad controls
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: causal-role classification dominates predictive control selection
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a strong predictor is also a collider or mediator
conflict_axes.example: controlling for a post-treatment variable that opens a biasing path

conflict_axes.trigger: stronger identifying assumptions enable point identification the data cannot verify
resolution_order: list testable implications of the assumed structure
test the implied conditional independences
weaken assumptions or add sensitivity analysis where untested
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: substantive knowledge plus testable implications dominate assumptions adopted for convenience
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a convenient DAG manufactures identification rejected by an implied-independence test
conflict_axes.example: drawing an arrow purely to justify a desired adjustment set

conflict_axes.trigger: the strongest design is infeasible or unethical, forcing a quasi-experimental fallback
resolution_order: check whether randomization is feasible and ethical
if yes randomize
if no select the quasi-experimental strategy matching the available variation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: feasibility and ethics dominate design strength; the best feasible identification is selected
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: randomization would withhold a beneficial or harmful treatment
conflict_axes.example: a policy cannot be randomized so DiD/IV/RDD is used instead

conflict_axes.trigger: a precise headline estimate competes with the doubt a sensitivity bound imposes
resolution_order: report the point estimate and its CI
report the sensitivity/robustness bound
present them jointly, never the estimate alone
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: robustness reporting dominates standalone precision; both must be shown
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a tight CI accompanies a small E-value
conflict_axes.example: publishing a narrow interval while hiding fragility to unmeasured confounding

conflict_axes.trigger: quasi-experimental designs identify local effects mistaken for population effects
resolution_order: state the estimand each design identifies
compare it to the decision's target estimand
reweight or qualify the claim to match
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the decision's target estimand dominates the convenient local estimand
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a LATE or cutoff-local effect is reported as the ATE
conflict_axes.example: interpreting an RDD's threshold-local effect as the average effect

conflict_axes.trigger: estimating mechanism components requires assumptions stronger than the total effect needs
resolution_order: confirm the total effect is identified
add mediation assumptions only if mechanism is the question
attach mediation sensitivity analysis
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the total-effect estimand dominates unless mechanism is explicitly the research question
conflict_axes.example: reporting indirect effects when only the total effect is identified

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to deliver an estimate competes with completing the identification argument
resolution_order: complete the identification argument first
then select and run the estimator
release only with documented assumptions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: identification rigor dominates delivery speed for any causal claim
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a stakeholder demands a number before identification is settled
conflict_axes.example: fitting a regression and calling its coefficient causal before checking assumptions

edge_cases.trigger: a causal claim is drawn from a covariate-adjusted observational estimate
edge_cases.failure_mode: unmeasured confounding read as a causal effect
edge_cases.example: reporting 'X causes Y' from adjusted observational data with no sensitivity bound
edge_cases.detection_method: check causal language against the identification strategy and sensitivity analysis
resolution: downgrade language to associational unless identified
add a sensitivity analysis or stronger design

edge_cases.trigger: a post-treatment variable is included in the adjustment set
edge_cases.failure_mode: over-control blocks part of the causal effect
edge_cases.example: controlling for a mediator and attenuating the true effect
edge_cases.detection_method: scan the control set for descendants of treatment
resolution: remove post-treatment bad controls
re-derive the backdoor adjustment set

edge_cases.trigger: conditioning on a common effect of treatment and outcome
edge_cases.failure_mode: collider bias creates a spurious association
edge_cases.example: including a collider in the propensity model
edge_cases.detection_method: check each conditioned variable for collider status on the DAG
resolution: drop the collider from the conditioning set
re-estimate after correcting the set

edge_cases.trigger: covariate strata have near-zero treatment probability
edge_cases.example: an IPW weight explodes because a propensity is near zero
edge_cases.detection_method: inspect the propensity-score distribution and common support
resolution: trim/restrict to the region of overlap
redefine the target population or estimand

edge_cases.failure_mode: weak-instrument bias toward the confounded estimate
edge_cases.example: a first-stage F well below conventional thresholds
edge_cases.detection_method: report first-stage strength and use weak-instrument-robust inference
resolution: use weak-IV-robust intervals
seek a stronger instrument or another design

edge_cases.trigger: treated and control groups have diverging pre-trends
edge_cases.failure_mode: DiD attributes a pre-existing trend to treatment
edge_cases.example: an event-study plot showing non-flat pre-period coefficients
edge_cases.detection_method: estimate and plot pre-treatment event-study coefficients
resolution: switch to synthetic control or a trend-robust estimator
restrict to a comparable control group

edge_cases.trigger: two-way fixed effects with heterogeneous, staggered treatment timing
edge_cases.failure_mode: negative-weight bias in the TWFE estimate
edge_cases.example: a TWFE estimate contaminated by already-treated comparisons
edge_cases.detection_method: decompose TWFE weights or use a heterogeneity-robust estimator
resolution: use a staggered-adoption robust estimator
report group-time effects

edge_cases.trigger: units manipulate the running variable around the cutoff
edge_cases.example: bunching just above the scholarship threshold
edge_cases.detection_method: run a McCrary density test at the cutoff
resolution: document and address manipulation
abandon RDD if sorting is confirmed

edge_cases.trigger: the synthetic control fails to match the pre-treatment trajectory
edge_cases.failure_mode: an invalid counterfactual inflates the estimated gap
edge_cases.example: large pre-treatment gaps between unit and synthetic control
edge_cases.detection_method: evaluate pre-treatment fit (RMSPE) and placebo gaps
resolution: respecify predictors/donor pool
report poor fit and withhold the causal claim

edge_cases.example: an unmeasured common cause of the mediator and outcome
edge_cases.detection_method: audit the DAG for unblocked mediator-outcome paths
resolution: control the confounder or use a method that allows it
attach a mediation sensitivity analysis

edge_cases.trigger: an internally valid effect is applied to a different target population without transport analysis
edge_cases.failure_mode: effect-modifier shift makes the transported claim wrong
edge_cases.example: applying a trial effect to a population with different effect modifiers
edge_cases.detection_method: compare effect-modifier distributions across source and target
resolution: reweight by effect modifiers and check overlap
restrict the claim to the studied population

workflow.objective: fix the causal estimand and its potential-outcomes contrast
acceptance_tests: estimand stated as a contrast on a named population
workflow.do_first_because: the estimand is the highest-coupling foundation every later choice inherits

workflow.objective: state identifying assumptions and encode them in a DAG
acceptance_tests: DAG acyclic with plausible common causes
workflow.do_first_because: identification must precede any estimator choice

workflow.objective: derive the adjustment strategy and a valid control set from the DAG
acceptance_tests: adjustment set blocks all backdoor paths
workflow.do_first_because: the control set must be fixed before any estimator runs

workflow.objective: select the identification/design strategy matching the available variation
workflow.do_first_because: strategy choice gates which estimator and diagnostics are valid

workflow.objective: build the adjustment estimator and verify balance/overlap
exit_criteria: estimator validated on balance and overlap
workflow.do_first_because: balance and overlap must pass before producing an estimate

workflow.objective: produce the point estimate with design-consistent uncertainty
acceptance_tests: uncertainty reflects clustering/bootstrap as the design requires
workflow.do_first_because: estimation can only follow a validated, identified estimator

workflow.objective: quantify robustness to unmeasured confounding and assumption violations
exit_criteria: sensitivity analysis attached to the estimate
workflow.do_first_because: no causal estimate is released without a robustness assessment

workflow.objective: optionally decompose mechanism and assess transport to the target population
exit_criteria: mechanism/transport analysis documented or explicitly deferred
workflow.do_first_because: mechanism and transport extend the claim only after the total effect is robust

workflow.objective: synthesize a defensible causal claim no stronger than identification allows and route high-risk decisions to human review
outputs: final causal claim with scope and caveats
acceptance_tests: claim scope matches the identified estimand
exit_criteria: claim approved for the stated estimand and population
workflow.do_first_because: the final claim must be reconciled against the original estimand and all assumptions

workflow.objective: route validation/sensitivity failures to repair, revalidate, and control changes
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem and repaired
workflow.do_first_because: iteration closes the loop so no downstream claim outlives a broken assumption

dominance_rules.trigger: a stakeholder demands an estimate before identification is settled
dominance_rules.rule: identification must be complete before any causal claim is issued
dominance_rules.required_action: block the causal claim until assumptions are documented
dominance_rules.example: refuse to label an unidentified coefficient causal

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value method is ordered before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: prerequisite nodes precede dependent ones regardless of importance
dominance_rules.required_action: reorder so the estimand and identification precede estimators
dominance_rules.example: do not run matching before the control set is fixed

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise estimate rests on a weak or unlabeled assumption
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade unsupported causal labels to associational
dominance_rules.example: relabel an adjusted association when ignorability is unjustified

dominance_rules.trigger: an estimate is ready to finalize but lacks a sensitivity analysis
dominance_rules.rule: no causal estimate is locked before a sensitivity analysis is attached
dominance_rules.required_action: block lock until robustness is quantified
dominance_rules.example: require an E-value before publishing an observational effect

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible causal decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automated acceptance for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: route the decision to a domain expert with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: escalate a policy-affecting causal claim to expert review

dominance_rules.trigger: randomization or a credible natural experiment is feasible
dominance_rules.rule: design-based identification dominates model-based adjustment when available
dominance_rules.example: choose an RCT over propensity adjustment when ethical and feasible

dominance_rules.trigger: the temptation to add more nodes/edges threatens schema consistency
dominance_rules.rule: schema consistency dominates adding more objects
dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding objects that break required structure
dominance_rules.example: keep node count within the dense band rather than padding

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting competes with strict JSON validity
dominance_rules.example: never wrap the KB in markdown fences

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks an eligible supporting source
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic and cite SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR
dominance_rules.example: do not assign observed labels without observed data

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence or feedback
dominance_rules.example: break a feedback loop with an explicit stop condition

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the estimand before choosing any estimator
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an estimator built for the wrong estimand answers the wrong question
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: estimator chosen before the contrast is defined
anti_rework_rules.example: fitting a model then deciding it estimates the ATT

anti_rework_rules.rationale: estimating before identification yields an uninterpretable number
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an estimate exists with no documented assumptions
anti_rework_rules.example: reporting a coefficient as causal before checking ignorability

anti_rework_rules.rule: build the DAG before selecting controls
anti_rework_rules.rationale: control selection without structure produces bad controls
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: controls chosen by predictive fit rather than the DAG
anti_rework_rules.example: kitchen-sink regression without a causal structure

anti_rework_rules.rationale: adjusting before role classification risks colliders/mediators
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a mediator or collider appears in the adjustment set
anti_rework_rules.example: including a post-treatment variable in the propensity model

anti_rework_rules.rationale: estimating without overlap yields extreme weights and undefined contrasts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: extreme weights or empty strata appear at estimation
anti_rework_rules.example: huge IPW weights from near-zero propensities

anti_rework_rules.rule: check parallel trends before trusting a DiD effect
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a DiD on diverging pre-trends attributes a trend to treatment
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a DiD effect reported with no event-study pre-period
anti_rework_rules.example: publishing a DiD without a pre-trend plot

anti_rework_rules.rule: select the design strategy before running its diagnostics
anti_rework_rules.rationale: strategy-specific diagnostics are wasted if the strategy changes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: diagnostics rerun after a late strategy switch
anti_rework_rules.example: running a McCrary test before deciding RDD applies

anti_rework_rules.rule: attach a sensitivity analysis before finalizing a causal claim
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a claim without robustness is retracted when a confounder is raised
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a final claim lacks any robustness bound
anti_rework_rules.example: releasing an observational effect with no E-value

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish the total effect before decomposing mechanism
anti_rework_rules.rationale: mechanism decomposition on an unidentified total effect is meaningless
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: direct/indirect effects reported without an identified total
anti_rework_rules.example: computing NDE/NIE before the total effect is valid

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking without traceability blocks safe later change
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock requested with incomplete traceability
anti_rework_rules.example: finalizing the KB before sources link to claims

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or design review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream blocking
action: score defects by risk_if_wrong and coupling
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix may affect dependent nodes/edges
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents of the changed object

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned to a subsystem
action: route the defect to its owner subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rerun the validator and formula computer

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a changed assumption shifts importance
action: flag nodes crossing the revisit delta
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no node exceeds the posterior revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is unresolved
acceptance_tests: human decision recorded for each high-risk item

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: diff against the prior version's checks
action: compare check results to the prior version

human_review_required_for: irreversible policy or treatment decisions informed by the effect
hard lock of the causal-claim protocol
adoption of an instrument or RDD whose key assumption is contested

checks.repair_action: split design/transport tradeoff into a conflict edge
recomputed derived fields via formula tool

test_cases.input_summary: does treatment X cause outcome Y
causal question with no randomization and likely unmeasured confounders
a policy turns on at a date in some units
treatment assigned by a cutoff on a running variable
apply a trial effect to a different population

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked identification or claim change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream assumption changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: hard lock of the causal-claim protocol
